checks.expected: Exactly the existing four named pairs/eight PDFs are selected; no discovered URL is enrolled.
All four readiness/pin/selected-source preflights finish before any HTTP execution starts.
Four serial batches preserve individual 4-request/4-URL/2MB-source/4MB-batch caps and total maximum16 requests/16MB response bytes; no retries.
Exit zero alone is not success: changed, partial, denied, not_checked and invalid reports remain distinguishable.
A changed valid PDF requires review and cannot update baselines, canonical files or legal status.
Immutable event/report artifacts survive failed jobs where execution reaches artifact handling; cancellation/platform upload failures remain explicit limits.
Workflow uses read-only repository permissions and checkout without persisted credentials; no commit, publication or deployment.
Finite wall timeout and per-batch/request deadlines remain effective; execution is serial and no hidden retry wrapper exists.
Only selected custody inputs are required, with no LFS fetch or whole-corpus completeness assumption.
Offline fixtures exercise unchanged, changed, partial/failure, refusal, preflight failure and report/exit disagreement; no live HTTP.
All hashes and imported dependencies refer to reviewed artifacts; original workspace paths are not required by installed runner.
Results assert transport/byte evidence only, not current law or source-wide extraction accuracy.

findings.statement: Final producer-status handling preserves valid stopped reports with otherwise complete observations as incomplete; denied/not-found/invalid/refused/partial source states remain explicit. Genuine report/exit disagreements and impossible completed-denial records are rejected.

The reviewer initially omitted the compile_report/verify_run invariant and incorrectly claimed that current completed reports could contain access_denied. That premise was withdrawn before any counterexample execution. The preserved history separates the valid stopped-plus-complete case from the impossible completed-denial case.

44 frozen author tests and 20 independent cases pass. An actual four-process readiness invocation passed against only88 pinned inputs, the70-row raw manifest, and the new runner/config in a different temporary root. Unselected missing originals were informational; no execute/verify-run mode or source runtime was created.

The workflow defaults to readiness only. Installation, default-branch presence, a Linux offline run, a separately approved finite live pilot and enabling scheduled GETs remain distinct. No Linux/GitHub-hosted execution, schedule activation, public HTTP or delivered alert is established by this audit.

The always-conditioned summary/upload steps preserve evidence when those steps execute. Job cancellation, timeout, runner loss or artifact-service failure can prevent upload;40minutes is the job limit,1200seconds covers only source-run windows. Read-only contents permission restricts GitHub API access, not filesystem writes; reviewed code confines its own writes to runtime directories.

Root requested a separate two-file compliance revision for test annotations and Markdown frontmatter after the154-payload preparation was sealed. This base audit preserves that sealed preparation unchanged; any later delta needs its own hashes and review.

limitations: Candidate-aware independent code review, with root/author feedback consulted; no blind or external model-diversity claim.
Fixture process responses do not establish real publisher access; actual readiness only reads retained local evidence.
Third-party versions are pinned through the requirements chain; this audit did not install or byte-audit package wheels.

The full author preparation is retained byte-identically. Eight selected source PDFs were verified in the working tree and copied only into a temporary sparse test corpus; the audit does not duplicate all canonical source bodies.
All64 focused cases were run locally on macOS/Python3.14.3. The 44-author-case runner coverage was measured; no full repository suite was rerun here.
